summary: Advance the existing plan to the researcher. The first review already accepted its scope and criteria; its minor stopping-rule ambiguity can be resolved during execution without another planning loop.
objective: Research manager: identify a bounded set of benchmark sources that can distinguish genuine information retention and revision from retrieving a longer transcript. Choose a feasible scope and stopping rule. Inspect sources only; do not install or execute code. Report canonical HTTPS links, what you actually inspected, each benchmark’s task and evaluation signal, whether it tests revision or only retrieval, limitations, and one comparison that could distinguish the competing explanations. Treat commissioning materials as leads, not independent findings.
content:
**Decision: advance.** The completed plan review approved a bounded scan of up to four primary benchmark sources, with research-only constraints and explicit reporting criteria. No researcher instance or findings are recorded yet.

Carry forward one small execution note: interpret “two successive query results” as two successive search queries, and record which queries yielded no new qualifying sources. This makes the stopping rule auditable without changing the plan. The researcher should also record any revision-testing gap if fewer than two inspected benchmarks test correction or updates. These issues will be documented in the evidence note; they do not block dispatch.
nextTask: Researcher: conduct the approved bounded source-discovery cycle. Inspect up to four primary benchmark sources; do not install or execute code. Record canonical HTTPS links, what you actually inspected, each benchmark’s task and evaluation signal, whether it tests revision/correction or retrieval only, and key limitations. Propose one controlled comparison to distinguish durable retention and revision from longer-transcript retrieval. Apply the stopping rule by treating successive query results as successive search queries; record which queries yielded no new qualifying source. If fewer than two sources test revision or correction, report that gap. Treat commissioning materials as leads, not independent findings.
